verdicts.note: Explicit forum statement that the ultra-wealthy need to be taxed and that the millionaire tax bill was 'drafted very well' [S6], echoed by pamphlet language against protecting the wealthy [S1]; the ESSB 6346 single-vote rule does not apply to a non-legislator's statements. +2 at medium fits.
'Universal healthcare solutions' without naming single-payer supports +1, not +2 [S3].

Lone-ESSB-6346 rule satisfied: ESSB 6346 nay plus independent nays on ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5801, co-sponsorship of tax-repeal bills HB 2130/HB 2335/HB 2167, and an explicit forum statement [S5][S6][S7][S13][S15]. -2/high stands.

Every spending signal in the dossier points to pole_a: nays on both operating budgets [S8][S9], a pledge to 'oppose reckless spending' and demand 'accountability' [S1], 'accountability for the tax dollars that fund our public schools' [S2], JLARC membership [S4], and co-sponsorship of HB 1225 on the budgeting process [S13]. Naming schools, special education, Medicaid and transportation as priorities when 'balancing the budget' [S15] is prioritization within restraint, not a call to expand. Nothing in the dossier pulls toward invest-and-expand, so the -1 hedge is not supported. -2/high, consistent with Ley (Pos. 2) on an equivalent record.
Single recorded vote (EHB 1217 nay) [S10]; -1/medium is the right magnitude for one vote.

Co-sponsorship of HB 1699 is a clear legislative act on sex-based sports eligibility [S13][S14], but it is the only social evidence (none on abortion or gender-affirming care). -1/medium holds; -2 would need a second topic or repeated statements.

The weight rests on one floor vote: the nay on ESHB 1296 [S11][S12]. That is a broad bill ('promoting a safe and supportive public education system', per the FBR) that only partly amends the I-2081 rights, so a nay is not purely a parental-rights vote. The second source, 'a champion for increasing parental involvement' in district decisions as a 2013-2017 school director [S3], is generic and says nothing about notification, record access or opt-outs. HB 1289 (school survey information) appears in the dossier without its content, so it adds nothing. As with the single-vote rule on taxes, one vote plus a generic statement supports -1/medium, not -2.

The dossier records only that she 'said differing state AI regulations create challenges for businesses' [S15]. Its Positions section does not record the scorer's 'better handled federally' framing; the cached article does report both candidates agreeing AI is better addressed federally. A worry about a state-by-state patchwork, with a preference for federal action, is not a position against regulating AI. Pole_a ('light-touch regulation') is inferred indirectly, so low.
